Operator 2026-10-21 (verbatim): "Make a research how ddflow could manage user requirements and user stories, for a project - make a deep research what are the best practices, what we do, what we plan to do, what can be reused, and make a phase and tasks proposal for the implementation with dependencies and wave set"

SCOPE: the USER-FACING layer only: user/business needs, personas, epics, stories, acceptance criteria, splitting, prioritisation, Definition of Ready/Done, release grouping, and the flow idea -> clarifying questions -> story -> readiness -> plan apply -> tasks -> verify criteria -> done. Siblings (link, do not duplicate): P-requirements (engineering standards, shipped requirement kind, D-requirements-*), P-product-docs (requirement record with EARS text, stakeholders, baselines, lint, trace, scoring, doc types), AP-stories (autopilot: stories -> a phase of tasks within a budget), P-specs (functional/technical specs, if filed by res-specs). Evidence and design: docs/ddflow/research/user-stories.md (task US-research).

data.body:
Ask the operator (clarifying-questions style: one batch, each with a recommended default) and file the decision document. Recommended defaults (research doc section 7): (1) a NEW data kind `story` with `level` = epic|story (two levels, a third `theme` is a label), NOT class=story on `requirement`: the lifecycle, hierarchy and criteria differ; it links to requirement records by `realises` and reuses every shared engine. (2) a persona is the shipped `stakeholder` kind with `class` = persona|person|group, no new kind. (3) acceptance criteria are structured entries INSIDE the story, addressable as S12#AC2, each with text (Given/When/Then, EARS or a plain testable sentence) and a verify (test node id, command, manual evidence or reviewer); not separate records. (4) stored status proposed|draft|ready|accepted|deferred|dropped; delivery status (unplanned|planned|building|verified) is DERIVED, never typed. (5) priority = MoSCoW (must|should|could|wont) + an operator-set rank within a release label; RICE/WSJF inputs stored and the score computed by PD-scoring, an agent cannot type a score. (6) Definition of Ready: persona + goal + 'so that' benefit + a source + at least one criterion + every criterion lint-clean + no open question + small enough; DoD: every criterion verified at the current tree by a recorded result, all linked tasks done, no suspect link, docs gate passed, a person accepted. (7) who may accept: a person; an agent only for the low-risk classes of requirements.agent_accept_classes (D-product-docs-r3) . (8) trackers: import first and file-based (JSON/CSV/markdown), one-way export later, ddflow stays the source of truth for criteria and verification; no live two-way sync in this phase. (9) injection: a story pack of at most [stories].charter_tokens (default 300) for the item being worked, never in the always-on charter. Record each settled choice with ddflow decision add.

ACCEPTANCE: The decisions are recorded with D- ids and the document exists; each recommended default is accepted, changed or rejected by the operator in his own words.

Data kind per D-record-surface-contract-r2; follow ddflow/templates/kinds/requirement.toml and stakeholder.toml; link fields to requirement (realises) and stakeholder (persona); [stories] knobs (charter_tokens, max_criteria, ready checks) in config_sections/stories.py.

ACCEPTANCE: A story added by `ddflow record story add` has history, search, recall, RAG export, supersede, split and an event-registry entry from the descriptor alone; the lifecycle rejects ready without a person; epic children point at their parent by id.

CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, rules r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core): every number is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; every definition this task adds is a record kind under the record contract RC1-RC12; shipped defaults overridable per project and per org; extend the shared engines instead of writing a second one; files under 20 KB. Evidence and design: docs/ddflow/research/user-stories.md. Siblings, not duplicated: P-requirements, P-product-docs, AP-stories, P-specs, P-sdd.



DESIGN NOTE (research section 7.1): the kind descriptor supports only string, array-of-strings and integer fields, so acceptance criteria are their OWN kind `criterion` (story link, form gherkin|ears|plain, text, verify, state proposed|agreed|verified|stale|dropped), not an array inside the story: per-criterion history, supersede, stale marking and PD-trace suspect links need record identity. `story add --criterion` creates them inline.
data.title: Story and criterion record kinds: story (level epic|story, persona, goal, benefit, realises, source, MoSCoW, rank, release, lifecycle) and criterion (form, text, verify, state), on the descriptor engine

data.body:
Pure parser (no I/O) in the style of services/plancheck.py. Forms: Gherkin (Given/When/Then/And), EARS (the five templates), plain testable sentence. Declarative-wording and one-behaviour-per-criterion checks live in US-lint, not here.

ACCEPTANCE: Gherkin, EARS and plain-sentence criteria parse to {id, form, text, verify, state}; ids survive edits and reordering; a malformed Given/When/Then is reported with the line.

CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, rules r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core): every number is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; every definition this task adds is a record kind under the record contract RC1-RC12; shipped defaults overridable per project and per org; extend the shared engines instead of writing a second one; files under 20 KB. Evidence and design: docs/ddflow/research/user-stories.md. Siblings, not duplicated: P-requirements, P-product-docs, AP-stories, P-specs, P-sdd.



NOTE: criteria are records of kind `criterion` (US-model); this task is the pure parser/normaliser of their text and verify fields, not their storage.
data.title: Acceptance criterion text: Given/When/Then, EARS and plain forms parsed to one shape, displayed ids S#n, verify spec grammar

data.body:
Ask the operator (clarifying-questions style: one batch, each with a recommended default) and file the decision document. Recommended defaults (research doc section 7): (1) a NEW data kind `story` with `level` = epic|story (two levels, a third `theme` is a label), NOT class=story on `requirement`: the lifecycle, hierarchy and criteria differ; it links to requirement records by `realises` and reuses every shared engine. (2) a persona is the shipped `stakeholder` kind with `class` = persona|person|group, no new kind. (3) acceptance criteria are structured entries INSIDE the story, addressable as S12#AC2, each with text (Given/When/Then, EARS or a plain testable sentence) and a verify (test node id, command, manual evidence or reviewer); not separate records. (4) stored status proposed|draft|ready|accepted|deferred|dropped; delivery status (unplanned|planned|building|verified) is DERIVED, never typed. (5) priority = MoSCoW (must|should|could|wont) + an operator-set rank within a release label; RICE/WSJF inputs stored and the score computed by PD-scoring, an agent cannot type a score. (6) Definition of Ready: persona + goal + 'so that' benefit + a source + at least one criterion + every criterion lint-clean + no open question + small enough; DoD: every criterion verified at the current tree by a recorded result, all linked tasks done, no suspect link, docs gate passed, a person accepted. (7) who may accept: a person; an agent only for the low-risk classes of requirements.agent_accept_classes (D-product-docs-r3) . (8) trackers: import first and file-based (JSON/CSV/markdown), one-way export later, ddflow stays the source of truth for criteria and verification; no live two-way sync in this phase. (9) injection: a story pack of at most [stories].charter_tokens (default 300) for the item being worked, never in the always-on charter. Record each settled choice with ddflow decision add.

ACCEPTANCE: The decisions are recorded with D- ids and the document exists; each recommended default is accepted, changed or rejected by the operator in his own words.

CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, rules r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core): every number is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; every definition this task adds is a record kind under the record contract RC1-RC12; shipped defaults overridable per project and per org; extend the shared engines instead of writing a second one; files under 20 KB. Evidence and design: docs/ddflow/research/user-stories.md. Siblings, not duplicated: P-requirements, P-product-docs, AP-stories, P-specs, P-sdd.



AMENDMENT (research section 7.1): decision (3) recommended default is now: acceptance criteria are their OWN small kind `criterion` (descriptor fields cannot hold structured objects; per-criterion history, stale marking and trace need record identity). Alternative to offer: an array of encoded one-line strings inside the story (cheaper, weaker). Also ask: (10) is a third level (theme/initiative) wanted beyond a label.

data.summary: MCP ddflow_task_add has no `kind` parameter although CLI `ddflow task add --kind task|doc|research|job` does: an MCP-only agent cannot file a doc/research task that runs the docs-only pipeline (CLI/MCP parity gap)
data.title: ddflow_task_add MCP lacks kind (CLI has --kind)

data.body:
Fixes bug Bmcp-task-add-no-kind: MCP ddflow_task_add has no `kind` parameter although CLI `ddflow task add --kind task|doc|research|job` does: an MCP-only agent cannot file a doc/research task that runs the docs-only pipeline (CLI/MCP parity gap) Found on US-research.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bmcp-task-add-no-kind --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bmcp-task-add-no-kind --regression-test <test>` first).

data.claim: ddflow has no story record, no tracker integration, and no acceptance-criterion verification; the only hooks are the inert requirement kind, the presence-only acceptance check in plan check, and the unexposed ask engine; descriptors cannot hold structured objects.
data.falsifier: A story/criterion/tracker module or a nested field type in ddflow/core/kinddata.py.
data.mechanism: Data kinds only allow string, array and integer fields; external sync reads sibling repo logs; bug regression verification is the only test-binding code.
data.probe: ddflow record requirement list; ddflow external --help; ddflow import --help; grep -n 'type = "' ddflow/templates/kinds/*.toml | sort | uniq -c; grep -rln 'services.ask' ddflow
data.probe_output: No requirement records.; external sync = observe the sibling-repo items needs names; import reads markdown checklists; field types: 18 array, 5 integer; services.ask referenced only by core/handlers/asks.py, approvals.py and ask/engine.py
